actual.value: No reporting as to the governance forum. Although IGAD hasn't held election observation mission, IGAD is having an ongoing engagement and collaboration with South Sudan National Election Commission.

actual.value:
No reporting as to the governance forum.

target.value: 100 % IGAD Member States adopt IGAD Governance, Democracy and Election Protocol ,100 % IGAD observation missions carried out in coordination with AU and other REC, IGAD governance platform becomes operational

actual.value: The draft Protocol has been presented to the IGAD Committee of Ambassadors but not endorsed by IGAD Head of States as there were no ordinary session in the reporting period. IGAD deployed two election observation missions in Uganda and Djibouti. The Election observation mission of Uganda was coordinated with the AU and East African Community. title.narrative: IGAD Governance, Democracy and Elections Protocol adopted by member states and IGAD’s election observation engagement enhanced

Adoption of IGAD Governance, Democracy and Elections Protocol by IGAD policy organs Number of Member States who develop action plan for implementation of IGAD Governance, Democracy and Elections Protocol Number of election observation missions deployed (for 2022-2023)

target.value: 1. All Member States adopt IGAD Governance. Democracy and Elections protocol 2. All Member States develop action plan to implement IGAD Governance. Democracy ad Elections protocol.

actual.value: According to IGAD this was not completed due to the fact that there were no ordinary sessions.

target.value: 1. Additional 2 Member States ratify IGAD Governance. Democracy and Elections protocol 2. Member States (2) supported to develop action plan for implementation the protocol

actual.value: Additional Member states did not ratify the IGAD Governance Democracy and Elections protocol in 2020.

target.value: One election observation mission deployed.

actual.value: IGAD deployed an election observation mission to Kenya to observe the 2022 general elections. 24 short-term observers (11 women). The short-term observers include representatives of electoral bodies and other public institutions as well as diplomats from 6 IGAD Member States: Djibouti, Ethiopia, Somalia, Sudan, South Sudan and Uganda.

target.value: Enhanced election observation experience in the Region.

actual.value:
IGAD is closely collaborating with South Sudan’s National Election Commission (NCE) and conducted an awareness creation and experience sharing conference on election management process from 29th – 31st May 2024 in Juba, South Sudan.
IGAD also conducted an experience sharing on election management convening 5 experts from each member states Election Management Bodies. The forum served as a learning platform for South Sudan National Election Commission as they prepare for the upcoming General elections later in the year.

target.value: Enhanced election observation experience in the Region.

actual.value: In the preliminary statement of the report, the IGAD Election Observation Mission commends the people of Djibouti for coming out to exercise their right to vote on 24th of February 2023 and doing so in an orderly, peaceful and non-violent manner. - June 9, 2023: IGAD Concludes a Roundtable Workshop for IGAD Member States’ Election Management Bodies (EMBs) on “Sharing of Experiences and Good Practices on Inclusive and Credible Elections”. Attended by UNSE, EAC. There were 25 attendees; of which 11 were women. - IGAD held election observation in Djibouti. 10 STOs deployed. IGAD first to issue report on election results. 5 women and 5 men.

target.value: 1. At least 2 Member states ratify IGAD Governance Democracy and Elections protocol 2. Member States (2) supported to develop action plan for implementation the protocol

actual.value: Member states have not ratified IGAD's Governance Democracy and Elections protocol.The Draft Protocol was expected to be endorsed by the IGAD Council of Ministers and then by Head of States and Governments, but there was no ordinary sessions of the Council of Ministers and head of states in the reporting period .

actual.value: PAP convened two rounds of consultation with IGAD Committee of Ambassadors on the draft Guidelines and Principles of the IGAD Governance Forum that has been validated by technical experts.

target.value: 1. IGAD Committee of Ambassadors adopt the platform 2. The regional governance Platform launched

actual.value: Policy organ under the Committee of Ambassadors of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) have reviewed and endorsed the Draft Guiding Principles and Rules of Procedure in order to establish the IGAD Governance Forum (IGF) that serves as a guiding policy framework and coordination mechanism for the promotion of good governance and democratic elections in the region. The launch was postponed.

target.value: All IGAD Member States agree on the guidelines and procedures for the operations of the platform

actual.value: Senior experts and officials of Member States have validated and approved the IGAD Governance Forum Guiding Principles and Rules of Procedures.

target.value: Member States’ institutions become part of the governance platform MoU signed between PAP and AU Governance Architecture Secretariat.

actual.value: The launch of the platform was expected to be held in March 2020. Due to the pandemic the Forum was put on hold in 2020 The launch took place on the 30th of April 2021 in Entebbe, Uganda. All member states democratic institutions (National Election Management Bodies, National Human Rights Institutions, Anti- Corruption Institutions, Ombudsman Intuitions and Judiciary are part of IGAD Governance Forum

title.narrative: Enhanced capacity of IGAD to effectively deploy and conduct preventive diplomacy and mediation
1. Number of IGAD Mediators and Technical Experts trained and readily available for deployment 2. Degree of intra and inter IGAD cooperation on mediation established and formalized through MoUs

target.value: Mediators trained and ready to take part in IGAD mediation.

actual.value: A consultative workshop was organized by IGAD, AU and OHCHR on the nexus between transitional justice and human rights in East Africa. The workshop brought transitional justice and human rights experts from the seven IGAD member states and explore the role OHCHR, IGAD and AU can play in conflict mediation, resolution and prevention of further violations.

target.value: The 21 mediators that were established in the roster trained and ready to take part in IGAD mediation

actual.value: April 2023: Three-day High-Level Workshop On Engaging The IGAD Roster Of Mediators And Experts On Crisis Response And Fact-Finding Missions, Djibouti. - June 15, 2023: IGAD’s Mediation Support Unit (MSU) concluded a three-day workshop in Rajaf, South Sudan. The workshop engaged CSOs to speak and engage women and youth in conflict resolution and negotiations. No mention of number of participants. - June 18, 2023: IGAD’s MSU concluded a three-day workshop in Nairobi, Kenya. The workshop brought together women, men, youth, and students who are refugees and IDPs in some of the horn of Africa (HOA) region. No mention of number of participants.

target.value: 100% Roster of Technical Experts trained and familiarized with IGAD Peace and Security programmes 2. Interface created and formalized between IGAD and AU on mediation and conflict resolution in the region

actual.value: IGAD MSU conducted for 22 roster of mediators gender responsive training for the roster of IGAD mediators to enhance their capacity in mainstreaming gender related issues during mediation process and in drafting peace agreements. IGAD MSU in consultation with 16 experts from Member States developed registration criteria, terms of engagement and structure, for establishing and managing a roster of technical experts. Based on the agreed criteria call for expression of interest was launched to identify andselect potential members of the roster of technical experts. The selection and establishment of the roster of technical experts will be finalized in the first half of 2020. AU, RECs/RMs coordination meeting was held in September 2019. AU, RECs/RMs Coordination meetings will be held biannually starting 2019 one at technical level and the other at strategic level.

target.value: 21 mediators that were established in the roster trained ready for deployment and to take part in IGAD mediation

actual.value: IGAD Mediation Support Unit organised a four-day training/ thinking workshop for Sudanese officials on negotiation and mediation skills. - Capacity Building workshop for women in refugee camps on mediation skills.

target.value: 1. IGAD Roster of Mediators and Technical Experts fully operational (100% assessed and ready for deployment) 2. All IGAD mandated mediations coordinated by MSU

actual.value: IGAD mainly supported the 2019-2020 Juba Peace Process of resolving the Sudan conflict.
